report:
Finding: Model B appears domain-shifted toward culinary/restaurant and “professional/technical” vocabulary and style.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens for the highest-norm cells are dominated by cooking/food terms and roles: “Cook, Cooking, restaurant/Restaurant, kitchen, Chef, baking, oven, microwave, Cake, culinary,” alongside “Professional/professional, Technical/technical, Engineering.” This cluster recurs across layers 19–25 and positions 1–4, not just sporadically.
- Earlier mid-layers also favor formal/academic/technical nouns (“dissertation, doctoral, sciences, petrochemical, metropolitan”), consistent with a shift toward more formal/professional register.
- The difference norm explodes in later layers (especially p1 at L21–L25), suggesting a high-level style/domain preference rather than low-level tokenization changes.

No Patchscope continuations were provided, but the logit-lens signal is strong and consistent: Model B is more likely to steer continuations toward culinary/restaurant content and professional/technical wording.
